text: His favourite room as a child was the family library: oak panelled, every wall lined with books. His father's Hebrew scholarship and all of Ibsen's plays. The young poets of the Great War, many of them killed. On the lowest shelves, where a small boy could reach, his older brothers' adventure books, including Kipling's Jungle Book: he identified with the wolf boy Mowgli. His mother's Dickens and Shaw. Medical books in a locked cabinet, with the key left in the door. He learned to read at three or four, and when he was late for a meal, the family knew where to look.
